newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Bk of East Asia may up HK$1.8 FRCD issue.
newsitem.headline: Bk of East Asia may up HK$1.8 FRCD issue.

text.p: Bank of East Asia said it may lift the size of its newly launched HK$1.8 billion three-year floating rate certificates of deposit (FRCD) issue to HK$2.5 billion.
Daniel Wan, the bank's deputy general manager, said the market's reception to the issue had been so good that the issue size may go above the initial amount of HK$1.8 billion.
The issue "may come up to HK$2.5 billion," Wan said, adding "we would like to see it come up to HK$2.5 billion."
Bank of East Asia on Thursday launched the three-year HK$1.8 billion bond, which pays an all-in return of 44 basis points to top-tier managers.
Wan said the purpose of the CD was to satisfy loan demand expected early next year.
The bank hopes to get the money by early December and made ready for loan drawdown in early 1997, Wan said.
He said the bank's loans grew about 20 percent in the first nine months of the year from the same period in 1995.
"We are thinking the Hong Kong economy is going to turn better and this is one of the reasons that why we are going for this issue now," said David Li, the bank's deputy chairman.
"We feel that there will be great demand for loans in the coming year," he added.
The bank issued a HK$2.0 billion FRCD in March.
